findings.title: Task 5 redeclares the online `lastGunSel` that W-4a already declares, so tsc fails
findings.claim: Decision 8 says W-4a's online branch has no `lastGunSel`, so Task 5 Step 5.2 adds `lastGunSel = 0` beside `weaponSel = 0, triggerPrev = false`. W-4a already declares it in that same `let` line, resets it everywhere, and updates it in the online Hound branch. The second declaration is a block-scoped redeclaration, which tsc rejects. Step 5.3 also replaces only the `nextWeaponSel` line, so W-4a's own `if (weaponSel !== WeaponSlot.Torpedo) lastGunSel = weaponSel;` stays and the line appears twice.
findings.evidence: Plan L100 ("W-4a's online branch has none: Task 5 adds it"), plan L934 (Step 5.2), plan L935-L941 (Step 5.3). The W-4a plan declares it in onlineDuel at L2140 (", weaponSel = 0, lastGunSel = 0, triggerPrev = false (the contract: both runtimes keep lastGunSel, which W-4c reads)"), resets it at L2142, and updates it at L2147-L2148.
findings.why: Task 5 cannot compile as written. Its tsc step (plan L951) fails.
findings.fix: Correct Decision 8: W-4a's online code already keeps `lastGunSel`. In Step 5.2 add only `, flight: FlightLatch = NO_FLIGHT, triggerLive = false`, and add only `flight = NO_FLIGHT; triggerLive = false;` to each reset. In Step 5.3 replace both of W-4a's lines (`weaponSel = nextWeaponSel(weaponSel, k, manualTorpedoFlying(d.tactical));` and `if (weaponSel !== WeaponSlot.Torpedo) lastGunSel = weaponSel;`) with the new block, as Step 4.3 already does for Single player.

findings.title: Task 6's controls-list test finds the Helm's 'Hold left mouse' row first, so it can never pass
findings.claim: The Single player rows already contain `{ keys: 'Hold left mouse', action: 'At the Helm, steer: the nose turns toward the pointer' }`, and it comes before the `Left click` row. Task 6 adds a second row with the same `keys` after `Left click`. The new test then does `rows.find((r) => r.keys === 'Hold left mouse')?.action).toMatch(/MANUAL torpedo.*steer/)`. `find` returns the Helm row, whose action does not match.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/app/controlsList.ts:L59 (the Helm's 'Hold left mouse' row, pushed before the L62-L65 mouse rows). Plan L996 (the assertion) and plan L1021 (the new row goes after `Left click`). Neither W-4a (L2371-L2386) nor W-4b changes the Helm row. tests/settingsAndControls.test.ts:L51 also reads `action('Hold left mouse')` and expects it to start with 'At the Helm'.
findings.why: The test stays red, and no rule covers it.
findings.fix: Keep the Helm row first, because settingsAndControls L51 needs it. Change the assertion to `expect(rows.filter((r) => r.keys === 'Hold left mouse').map((r) => r.action)).toContainEqual(expect.stringMatching(/^At Weapons, with a MANUAL torpedo flying: steer it/))`. Alternatively, give the new row distinct keys such as 'Hold left mouse (Weapons)' and find by those.

findings.title: Task 7's `canonical-trace.ts golden` has no basic.json copy to compare, because no task records the canonical baseline before it
findings.claim: `canonical-trace.ts golden` reads `basicCopy`, which only `canonical-trace.ts baseline` writes, and it throws when the copy is missing. Neither W-4c Task 1, W-4a nor W-4b runs `canonical-trace.ts baseline`. The first W-4c run is Task 8 Step 2, which comes after Task 7. The temp dir is keyed by the worktree root, so a fresh worktree has no copy. Task 7 Step 2 therefore throws ("no copy of tests/golden/basic.json … run the baseline before the bump").
findings.evidence: Plan L1067-L1068 (Task 7 Step 2). Plan L136-L139 (Task 1 Step 3 records only the duel-oracle baseline). scripts/golden/canonical-trace.ts:L16-L21 (baseline writes basicCopy) and L30-L31 (golden throws without it). scripts/golden/versionOnly.ts:L30 (`dirFor(root)` per checkout). A grep of the W-4a and W-4b plans finds no `canonical-trace` call.
findings.why: Task 7 fails as written. If a stale copy exists instead, the check compares against an unknown commit.
findings.fix: In Task 1 Step 3 also run `npx tsx scripts/golden/canonical-trace.ts baseline`, note its counts, and add it to the report. In Task 7 Step 1 also run `npx tsx scripts/golden/canonical-trace.ts same`, the sector per-tick proof that W-4c moved nothing, then keep the `golden` check after the bless. Add the same missing-baseline fallback that Step 1 already has.

findings.title: Task 5 anchors the Single player edits on W-4a's code, which W-4b changes; read literally, the edit drops W-4b's MAN gate on the held trigger
findings.claim: Step 4.5 says W-4a's merge `weaponsSeatHeld(weaponSel, deps.triggerHeld?.() ?? false)` becomes `weaponsSeatHeld(weaponSel, triggerLive)`, keeping a `turretAim` part if W-4b added one. W-4b actually rewrites that call as `weaponsSeatHeld(weaponSel, (deps.triggerHeld?.() ?? false) && gunModeBase(), deps.reticleAim?.() ?? -1)`. An executor who puts `triggerLive` in place of the trigger expression drops `&& gunModeBase()`, so AUTO sends `gunHeld` again. Step 4.4 likewise quotes `if (pew !== null && weaponSel === WeaponSlot.Pew) {`, which W-4b changes to `… && gunsManual) {`.
findings.evidence: Plan L924-L928 (Step 4.4-4.5). The W-4b plan rewrites the merge at L1040 and the pew click at L1038. W-4b's test at L905-L916 ('in AUTO the held trigger puts no gunHeld') would fail. W-4b Decision 7 is at L65.
findings.why: This is an edit that won't match the post-W-4b code. Two executors would build it differently, and one way breaks W-4b's AUTO rule and its test.
findings.fix: Quote W-4b's text. The merge becomes `weaponsSeatHeld(weaponSel, triggerLive && gunModeBase(), deps.reticleAim?.() ?? -1)`. The pew click becomes `if (click !== null && weaponSel === WeaponSlot.Pew && gunsManual) {`. The dead-trigger line keeps W-4b's `&& gunsManual` and reads `trig = triggerLive`.

findings.title: Task 5's online test cases name a rig that has no session, and case 3 cannot pass as described
findings.claim:
The online describe is told to use 'the `tests/w4Online.test.ts` rig'. That file is unit-level: `sessionHeld` cases and W-4b's `rig(sel, aim)`, which returns `{d, held, gunnerHeld}` with no session, client or source. The session cases (`r.d`, `c.helds()`, `h.sources`) live in `tests/onlineDuelSession.test.ts`'s `rig(1)`. Three further problems:
- That rig's replica is a snapshot copy, so 'removing it from the replica' needs `removeMissile(r.d.tactical, 0); r.client().publish(r.d)`.
- `unacked(5)` is no test API: the stub's `heldHighWater` stays [0, 0], so k grows with every pump.
- Case 3 uses `turret(1)` on the autocannon, which starts with 0 bars, so `predictTurret` returns the replica's value with or without a flight. 'Differs once it is gone' fails.
findings.evidence: Plan L863-L866. The W-4a plan's w4Online is at L2078-L2104 and its session cases at L2107. W-4b's w4Online `rig(sel, aim)` is at L1426-L1433 and its session prediction case at L1462-L1477. tests/onlineDuelSession.test.ts:L38-L42 (publish copies through a snapshot, `heldHighWater: [0, 0]`) and L110-L143 (rig). W-4b's predictTurret returns `base` when bars < 1 (L1498-L1499). Start power is 1 / 0 / 1.
findings.why: An executor cannot write these cases as specified, and case 3 as worded stays red.

findings.title: Task 2 misses the `torpTurn` uses in manualTorpedoFlight's 'keeps the mode it launched with' case
findings.claim: Step 1 rewrites only the 'flies a MANUAL torpedo…' case and the `manualTorpTurn` calls. The next case still steps `{ ...IDLE_INPUT, torpTurn: 1 }` twice. Once `torpTurn` leaves `ShipInput`, those literals fail tsc's excess-property check. At runtime the MANUAL torpedo would no longer turn, so `[m.manual, m.heading]` would read `[true, 0]` instead of W-3's number. The catch-all at L297 only covers 'any other file'.
findings.evidence: tests/manualTorpedoFlight.test.ts:L105 and L113 (`{ ...IDLE_INPUT, torpTurn: 1 }`), with the expectation at L107. Plan L190-L208.
findings.why: tsc and that case stay red until an executor notices. Spec §14 says W-3's flight tests keep their numbers.
findings.fix: Add to Step 1: in 'keeps the mode it launched with', `{ ...IDLE_INPUT, torpTurn: 1 }` becomes `{ ...IDLE_INPUT, torpHeading: 64 }` at L105 and L113, and the expectations stay (holdTurn toward 64 from 0 is +1 a tick, as `torpTurn: 1` was). Also update the file header (L3-L4, 'A and D turn it') and manualTorpedoInput's header (L4-L5) to cite W-4 spec §7.

findings.title: The import-cycle guard in Task 3 checks the wrong edge
findings.claim: Step 4 says to inline the check 'if `hunter.ts` imports `turret.ts`'. It doesn't. The cycle comes through weapons.ts: turret.ts → manualTorpedo.ts → hunter.ts → weapons.ts (which imports `slewTurrets` from turret.ts after W-4b) → turret.ts. The condition is false, so the executor adds the import and creates a new cycle. It is harmless at runtime (only call-time uses), but the plan's own stated intent ('no import cycle') is missed.
findings.evidence: Plan L572. src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/hunter.ts:L16 (imports weapons). manualTorpedo.ts:L4 (imports hunter). The W-4b plan's L815 has weapons.ts import turret.ts.
findings.why: The instruction is ambiguous and defeats its own goal.
findings.fix: Always inline `missileOf(state, i)?.manual === true` in turret.ts (`missileOf` comes from state.ts, which turret.ts already uses), with the W-4 spec §3.4/§7 comment.

findings.title: Decision 8 returns the selection when the torpedo is selected at the flight's end; the spec says 'selected at launch'
findings.claim:
Spec §7 says: 'If the torpedo was selected at launch, the selection returns to the last gun selected.' `flightFrame` tests `sel === WeaponSlot.Torpedo` on the end frame. Because A/D now select during a flight, the two rules differ in two cases:
- launched with F on pew, then 3 pressed mid-flight: the plan returns it, the spec does not;
- launched with the torpedo selected, then A mid-flight: the two outcomes coincide.
The deviation is not flagged as one.
findings.evidence: Spec L387-L390. Plan L100 and L893.
findings.why: This is a small spec drift. The spec's only firm requirement is that control returns to the selected gun, which the plan's rule satisfies.
findings.fix: State the choice as a deviation in Decision 8 ('at the end, not at launch: A/D select during the flight, so the selection at the end is the gunner's latest intent'), or record the selection in the latch at launch.
